identity.name: Sodium propionate
identity.chemical_class: Sodium salt of propionic acid (short-chain fatty acid salt)

function.mechanism: Weak-acid preservative salt that inhibits mold/spoilage growth, especially in bakery-type foods; also used as a flavoring agent under GMP conditions.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for propionic acid and its salts (including E281).

efsa.key_finding: 2014 re-evaluation found no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/levels; 2016 E281 use-extension opinion found no safety concern at proposed uses/levels.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI is NOT LIMITED (group ADI for propionic acid and calcium/potassium/sodium salts).

concerns.summary: Human challenge studies and translational work reported propionate-associated increases in counter-regulatory hormones (e.g., glucagon/catecholamine-related signals) with insulin-resistance/hyperinsulinemia markers under study conditions.
Zebrafish embryo study reported altered behavior, circadian-gene disturbances, and glucose-metabolism/insulin-resistance-related developmental effects after sodium propionate exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation did not identify safety concern at reported uses/levels and did not require a numerical ADI.
JECFA assigned group ADI as NOT LIMITED for propionic acid and calcium/potassium/sodium salts.
US FDA CFR affirms GRAS status under GMP conditions of use.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported relatively higher exposure estimates in toddlers/children, but EFSA and JECFA benchmarks are non-numerical (no numerical ADI / not limited), so classical ADI exceedance is not directly applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory assessments remain permissive (EFSA no numerical ADI; JECFA not limited; FDA GRAS), but mechanistic and intervention studies show non-trivial metabolic signaling concerns under specific exposure conditions.
key_factors: EFSA 2014 re-evaluation: no numerical ADI needed
EFSA 2016 opinion: no safety concern for proposed E281 extension uses
FDA GRAS affirmation in 21 CFR 184.1784 under GMP
JECFA ADI NOT LIMITED, maintained at 49th meeting
Human/animal mechanistic studies report metabolic-endocrine perturbation signals
